summary.value: Pagination component, used to navigate through a list of items.

value.rule: Use pagination when content must be divided across multiple pages, users need to know their position within the set, and loading everything at once would hurt performance
value.quote: Use pagination when search results or large amounts of data need to be divided across multiple pages users need to understand where they are within a larger set of content loading the entire dataset at once would be too heavy or result in poor performance

value.rule: Avoid pagination when content fits on a single page, when paging a form, or when progress needs to be shown
value.quote: Avoid pagination when the total amount of content is small enough to fit on a single page you want to divide a form into several pages progress needs to be displayed

value.rule: On mobile, show fewer page buttons and drop the previous/next text labels
value.quote: On mobile devices, you can show fewer pages and remove the text for previous/next.

value.rule: Use pagination when content is too large for one page and users need to navigate back and forth
value.quote: Use pagination when content is too large for a single page, such as search results or long lists, and the user needs to navigate back and forth.

value.rule: Only split content across multiple pages if doing so improves loading time or usability
value.quote: Content should only be split across multiple pages if it improves loading time or usability.

value.rule: Use the fixed text pattern "Previous"/"Next"; avoid alternate wordings like "Previous page", "Go back", "Continue"
value.quote: We use a fixed pattern for pagination with the words “Previous” and “Next”. Avoid “Previous page”, “Next page”, “Go back”, “Go forward”, “Continue” and “Back”.
